summary.text: Ben Keathley is a Republican state representative and attorney from Chesterfield, Missouri, who has represented House District 101 since January 2023 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
He faces Democrat Paul Lentz and Libertarian Jeff Coleman.

paragraphs.text: Keathley lives in Chesterfield, Missouri, and graduated from Marquette High School. He earned a bachelor's degree in Latin and political science from Knox College in 2009, and a master's degree in political science and government and a J.D. from Syracuse University in 2013.
His career experience includes working as an attorney in private practice, and he served two terms on the Chesterfield City Council.
Keathley won the District 101 seat in 2022, defeating Melissa Greenstein and Jeff Coleman, assumed office on January 4, 2023, and won re-election in 2024 over Jacqueline Cotton.
His 2025-2026 committee assignments are General Laws, which he chairs, Judiciary, Legislative Review, and the Joint Committee on Administrative Rules, which he chairs.
